1.title: Strip about a centimetre off ends
1.say: Push one wire end into the stripper. Squeeze the stripper on the held end, so bare metal shows. Do the same for the other wire.
placements: end of one wire → inside stripping tool jaws about one centimetre from tip, in the video: wire on right side
end of other wire → inside stripping tool jaws about one centimetre from tip, in the video: wire on left side
watch_for: if bare metal looks nicked or cut, you squeezed too hard.
if coating still covers the tip, peel a little more off.
1.check_yourself: It should look like two loose ends with shiny bare tips.
1.safety: Keep fingers clear of the stripping jaws.

2.title: Twist bare ends together tight
2.say: Push the two bare ends together end to end. Twist the bare ends round, so they lock.
placements: bare end of wire on left → overlapped end to end with bare end of wire on right at centre, in the video: bottom of loop
bare ends of both wires → twisted round each other tight to lock, in the video: small twist at bottom of loop
watch_for: if join pulls apart, twist tighter round each other.
if sharp tips stick out, tuck them flat to the twist.
2.check_yourself: It should look like one loop with a small neat twist.

3.title: Coat join with cleaning paste
3.say: Touch the stick to the cleaning paste. Wipe the paste called flux onto the twist.
placements: cleaning paste called flux on tip of small stick → wiped all over bare twist at centre, in the video: bottom of loop
small stick → touched to bare twist then lifted away, in the video: held from top
watch_for: if twist looks dry, add another dab to wet it all over.
if paste sits on coating, wipe it onto bare metal only.
3.check_yourself: It should look like a wet shiny twist in the middle.

4.title: Melt solder over the join
4.say: Melt a little solder onto the hot tip. Hold the hot tip against the bare twist. Touch solder wire to the twist, so it spreads along.
placements: tip of soldering iron with melted solder on it → held against bare twist at centre, in the video: iron from top onto bottom of loop
thin solder wire → touched to heated twist beside iron tip until it spreads along, in the video: fed from right side
watch_for: if solder balls up, the twist was not hot enough.
if bare metal still shows, touch on a little more solder.
4.check_yourself: It should look like the twist coated shiny solder.
4.safety: Do not touch the hot tip or fresh solder.

5.title: Slide tube over the join
5.say: Push the short tube onto one wire end. Slide the tube along to the shiny join. Center the tube to overlap coating both sides.
placements: short insulating tube → pushed onto free end of one wire, in the video: threaded from top end
short insulating tube → slid along to centre over shiny join overlapping coating both sides, in the video: bottom of loop
watch_for: if shiny metal shows past tube, use a longer tube.
if tube sits to one side, slide it to centre it.
5.check_yourself: It should look like a loose tube over the join.
5.safety: Let the shiny join cool before touching it.

6.title: Shrink tube tight with heat
6.say: Hold the hot air nozzle near the tube. Move heat slowly along the tube. Lift heat away once it grips tight.
placements: mouth of hot air tool → held just above tube and moved slowly along it, in the video: metal tool from top
insulating tube → shrunk tight around wire by heat all round, in the video: tight band at bottom of loop
watch_for: if coating bubbles or browns, hold heat farther away.
if tube stays loose, heat a little longer all round.
6.check_yourself: It should look like a tight pinched band around wire.
6.safety: Do not touch the hot nozzle or tube.
